title: Quant interop gating log — week of 2026-02-25
summary: Weekly research notes focused on gating criteria for int4 quantized model onboarding, interoperability with KV cache layout changes, and short-term eval failures. Key outcome: definition of a conservative rollout gate and three concrete follow-ups.
notes:
Meeting date: 2026-02-25

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel, Elena Ruiz, Samir Bose, Priya Nair, + SRE on-call (recording attached in linked_artifacts).

Purpose: capture current state of quantization + runtime interop testing, triage recent eval regressions, and set gating criteria for onboarding the v2-int4 variant into dedicated serving pools.

Context / background:
- Recent model candidate (redwood-v2-large-int4) shows promising cost reduction but has divergent failure modes when combined with a new KV cache layout introduced in runtime PR 4823.
- We need a low-risk rollout plan for Dedicated and Hosted that prevents customer-visible regressions while letting us gather traffic.

Summary of experiments run this week (sanity + targeted probes):
1) Sanity throughput sweep (local 4xA100 replica):
   - float16 baseline (v2-lr): 1200 tokens/s single-replica (seq=512, batch=1)
   - int4 candidate (no KV change): 2180 tokens/s (≈+82% throughput), p95 latency 86ms
   - int4 + new KV layout (runtime PR 4823): 2100 tokens/s, p95 latency 92ms (slight overhead)
2) Coherence probe (30k sample prompts from eval set 'r4k-labs'):
   - automated rouge/alpha metrics: int4 delta vs f16: -0.9% on answer overlap; int4+KV delta: -1.4%
   - failure modes: hallucination spike on multi-step instruction prompts; high variance on numeric-extraction tasks
3) Cache stress test (mixed short/long prefixes):
   - KV prefetch + int4: reduced token generation cost by ~38% under 80% cache hit scenarios, but observed 0.6% increase in top-1 generation divergence for prompts that exercise long-term memory retrieval
4) A/B mimic on small internal canary (synthetic traffic mirroring PLG-tier):
   - Error budget burn: acceptable for 48 hours (errors within thresholds), but one traffic class (large-context code-completion) showed doubled timeout rate when int4 + new KV were combined.

Triage notes (why some evals regressed):
- Suspected root causes: rounding amplification in attention kernels interacting with a change to KV pack padding. The padding introduced misaligned residual magnitude for very long prefix chains, which the int4 quantization accentuates.
- Reproduction: deterministic repro found for a subset of prompts with >1024 prefix tokens and repeated attention to the same memory key. Repro snippet attached to PR 4823.
- Quick workaround: fall back to f16 for requests flagged as "long-prefix" at request-time (heuristic: total_prefix_tokens > 1024 OR user-specified context_mode: 'retrieval-heavy').

Decisions / gating criteria agreed (conservative rollout):
- Gate 1 (quality): end-to-end automated eval delta must be <= 0.5% absolute on core production eval suites (Q/A, summarization, numeric extraction). Currently not met -> additional fixes needed.
- Gate 2 (latency & SLO): p95 must be within 20% of f16 baseline for the same configuration and load profile. Passed in baseline tests but needs verification across cloud regions.
- Gate 3 (error budget): no traffic class should show >2x increase in timeout/error rate during a 72h synthetic canary. Currently one class failed — block.
- Gate 4 (rollback policy): canary rollout must support automatic revert to f16 variant per-route and per-customer and expose a single click rollback in control plane. Implementation ticket: MLINF-1287.

Action items (owners + ETA):
1) Arjun Patel — instrumented kernel-level debug traces for attention rounding (PR branch: arjun/attn-quant-trace). ETA: 2026-03-03.
2) Elena Ruiz — implement runtime heuristic to detect long-prefix requests and route them to f16 fallback; add unit tests. ETA: 2026-03-05.
3) Samir Bose — extend canary harness to run cross-region p95 sweeps and the code-completion traffic class; add alerting for doubling timeouts. ETA: 2026-03-08.
4) Maya Chen — assemble a short eval deck for leadership with clear pass/fail thresholds and cost savings estimate; include conservative and aggressive rollout scenarios. ETA: 2026-03-09.
5) Priya Nair — run more focused evals on numeric-extraction suite with and without KV padding changes to quantify regression surface. ETA: 2026-03-04.

Open questions / discussion items for next meeting:
- Is the long-prefix heuristic too coarse? risk of over-routing (cost regressions) — need sample of production traffic to estimate percent of routed-away requests.
- Should we try an alternate padding strategy (zero vs learned pad token) in runtime to reduce residual skew? Tradeoff: increases kernel complexity.
- Quantization schedule: do we gate int4 onboarding for Hosted entirely until interop fixes? or allow Dedicated enterprise customers to opt-in behind a feature flag?

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customer-visible regressions in retrieval-heavy flows. Mitigation: conservative fallback + targeted canary to those enterprise pools first.
- Risk: hidden drift in downstream metrics (rerank precision). Mitigation: expand eval suites to include rerank and user-intent signals for next run.

Quick wins identified:
- Add a tiny bit of jitter to KV packing alignment to avoid pathological alignment collisions (low-effort kernel change) — Arjun to prototype.
- Add a fast heuristic in inference layer to detect repeated-key attention and prefer safer kernels.

Notes to self / rough todos (not blockers for others):
- Collect 24h of production logs for the 'code-completion' traffic class for baseline distribution of prefix lengths (requested from SRE).
- Draft blurb for customer-facing release notes explaining opt-in behavior and fallback safety nets.

Next sync: 2026-03-04 10:00 PST (15m). Goal: verify Arjun and Elena progress, re-run canary after fixes.

Appendix (short reproduction pointer):
- Minimal repro: see gist in PR 4823 (lines 84-112). Steps: 1) seed model with 1100 token prefix consisting of repeated retrieval keys, 2) request generation length 256, 3) run with int4+KV pack. Observable metric: confidence collapse and hallucination after token ~120.
- Local perf harness commands: ./tools/perf_sweep --model redwood-v2-large-int4 --kv-layout new --seq 512 --batch 1
